text:
Pierre-Luc Dubois has quietly been one of the better parts of Washington's season. After playing only 29 games last year, he has 13 points in 17 games and Washington takes 58% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, six points better than without him. He's been finishing too: 5 goals in his last ten games, including a power-play goal in Boston last Saturday.

That last bit is where we'd temper it. He's scoring on 18% of his shots against an expected range of 11 to 17%, and our numbers have him 1.5 goals ahead of his chances. The assists dried up over the same stretch (one in ten games), so the points may even out in a different shape.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a useful habit: he carried the puck in on 71% of his entries last season, though that was only seven tracked games. Small samples run through his whole profile after last year. For a Capitals team that has lost seven of ten, a healthy, productive Dubois is one of the few things going right.
